subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class bootstrap context selector and dynamic command-expansion contract for session-specific context, and which slice should be accepted first?
rationale: The request spans user-facing config, session-state semantics, and a command-execution security boundary, while current open PRs implement only partial slices that need a shared direction.

options.title: Ship selector/tier first
options.body: Accept a narrow configurable selector or bootstrap-tier contract that preserves current defaults and leaves command expansion for a separate security design.

options.title: Use hooks only
options.body: Keep core fixed and require bootstrap-extra-files or plugin hooks to handle custom context, accepting that session-type filtering remains less discoverable and less deterministic.

options.title: Design full command expansion
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers approve a sandboxed dynamic command-expansion model with provenance, opt-in config, and tests.

recommendation.title: Ship selector/tier first
recommendation.body: Accept a narrow configurable selector or bootstrap-tier contract that preserves current defaults and leaves command expansion for a separate security design.

likelyOwner.reason: The historical subagent bootstrap limiting work makes this owner the strongest available routing signal for the selector/defaults decision.
